relevance_note: A 2017 PID review that summarises one previously published TNFAIP3 patient with individual-level features: 'an infant with lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly and persistent fever, Takagi et al.^37 found a biallelic mutation in the TNFAIP3 (HA20) gene'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short script only assembled the JSON. The paper is a general primary-immunodeficiency review; TNFAIP3 appears in one paragraph and Table 5. Zhou et al.^36 ('six unrelated families') and the cohort studies ^38,39 are described only at group level, so they get no rows. The one in-scope person is the Takagi et al.^37 infant (label rule 4). No variant description is printed, so variant_original_string is 'not reported'. The paper calls the mutation 'biallelic' without saying homozygous or compound heterozygous, so zygosity is 'not reported'; note that the cited reference title reads 'Haploinsufficiency of TNFAIP3 (A20) by germline mutation', which sits uneasily with 'biallelic', and Table 5 gives TNFAIP3 'Autosomal Dominant' at gene level (not used for this person). 'predicting a truncated protein' is not mapped to a variant class. 'persistent fever' was not taken as 'recurrent fever' on the checklist. 'infant' was recorded as age at diagnosis because it is the age at WES. is_proband and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients are left null: this is a review, and the reference for the person is in source_reference_in_review.

span: Phosphorylation of IKK and NF-κB was increased in patient-derived T cells.
Mutant TNFAIP3 (HA20)–transfected cells showed increased TRAF6 polyubiquitination, suggesting the loss of TNFAIP3 (A20) deubiquitination activity.
